title: Make the offer
principles: P05 Build your empire; P03 Develop your killer instinct (revisited)
model: M06 Second-order consequences and M08 Feedback loops, applied
evidence: An offer sheet with scope, costs and an explicit ask

say: You know your audience, their problem, your lever and your signal. Now you put something in front of them and ask for a commitment.
This is the lesson where the empire meets the market.

scenes.lead: "Let me know if I can help."
scenes.headline: WHAT ARE YOU *ACTUALLY* OFFERING?
say: Let me know if I can help. Happy to chat any time. Reach out if you need anything.
These sound generous. They ask nothing and offer nothing specific, so they usually produce nothing at all.

scenes.text: An offer someone can say yes to has edges. They know what they get, what it costs and what you need from them.
say: A real offer has edges. The result they will get. The scope: what is included and what is not. The time it takes. The cost, in money or effort. And the specific commitment you are asking for.
When an offer has edges, people can say yes to it. Or no, which is also useful.
Here is the rule for this week. A small, clear offer beats a big, vague promise.
You can always expand a pilot that works. You cannot easily shrink a promise you made to everyone.
Kofi is a skilled joiner who has built a simple system for organising small workshops. His first instinct is to tell local businesses he can help any of them get organised.
Instead he builds an offer with edges.

scenes.kicker: Three ways to put it into the world

cols.title: The open promise
cols.text: Help everyone with everything. Nobody replies.

cols.title: Give it all away
cols.text: Unlimited help, no review. Resentment by week three.

cols.title: The bounded offer
cols.text: Four weeks, one workshop, fixed fee, review on day 28.

scenes.quote: Four weeks, one workshop, a fixed fee. We review on day twenty-eight and decide together whether to continue.
say: Three ways to make the offer.
The open promise. I can help any business with anything. It sounds big and nobody replies, because nobody knows what they would be agreeing to.
Give it all away. Unlimited help, no fee, no end date. By week three he resents the client and the client has no reason to value the work.
The bounded pilot. Four weeks, one workshop, a fixed fee and a review on day twenty-eight where they decide together whether to continue.
This uses everything from week four. The pilot holds the line on price, and the review date is a planned decision point, so either side can continue or withdraw cleanly.

scenes.headline: Every response *teaches you something.*

items.label: Commitment
items.text: They agreed to the ask. Deliver and review.

items.label: Information
items.text: Ask why, if appropriate. Adjust the offer.

items.label: Silence
items.text: One proportionate follow-up. Then record it as data.

say: Every response counts as evidence. A yes is a commitment to deliver. A no is information about fit, price or timing. Silence gets one polite follow-up, and then it is recorded as data too.
Your pass in this course never depends on someone saying yes. It depends on making a clear offer and learning honestly from what happens.

scenes.headline: BUILD YOUR OFFER SHEET.
items: The result, in one sentence they would use.
Scope: what is in and what is out.
The exact commitment you will ask for.
say: Pause the video when I tell you to.
One. The result, in one sentence your audience would use.
Two. The scope: what is included and what is not.
Three. The time and cost, stated plainly.
Four. The exact commitment you will ask for. Pause now and give it five minutes.

rows: Result, scope, time, cost and ask.
Offer sheet with an explicit ask.
say: Your mission is workbook page W05-D03, construct the offer.
Prepare your offer sheet. Tomorrow you put it in front of the people it is for.

scenes.give: Make it clear. Make it today.
say: That completes week five. On Saturday the Council asks you to defend the value of what you built.
Then the final week: become dangerous.
Nobody can accept an offer you never made. Make it clear, and make it today.

notes: No income claims. The pilot fee is illustrative and participants set their own terms.
Revenue is optional in this course; a participation invitation or free release with an explicit ask is equally valid.
